This guide collects material for writing reports, papers, and slides that combine text and R code in R Markdown. Begin with the three picks under Start here, then use the sections on citations, templates, and output formats as your project needs them. PDF output needs a LaTeX installation; the [TinyTeX](../tinytex.html) page links to the easy setup, and the [R](../r.html) page covers installing R.

## Start here

- [Posit Documentation on RMarkdown](https://rmarkdown.rstudio.com/lesson-1.html) — First lesson of Posit's R Markdown tutorial. RMarkdown uses Pandoc's implementation of Markdown (see the Pandoc entry below).
- [R Markdown: The Definitive Guide (2023)](https://pkg.yihui.org/rmarkdown-book/) — Reference book covering R Markdown's output formats, options, and features.
- [R Markdown Cookbook (2024)](https://pkg.yihui.org/rmarkdown-cookbook/) — Task-based follow-up to the Definitive Guide, for more advanced work.

## Learning R Markdown

- [Pandoc's Markdown](https://pandoc.org/MANUAL.html#pandocs-markdown) — Section of the Pandoc manual describing the Markdown syntax that R Markdown documents are written in.
- [RMarkdown for Scientists](https://rmd4sci.njtierney.com/) — Online book created for a three-hour workshop on R Markdown.
- [Introduction to R Markdown (2019)](https://rpubs.com/brandonkopp/intro_to_r_markdown) — Introductory R Markdown tutorial published on RPubs in 2019.
- [Writing reproducible reports in R with markdown, knitr and pandoc](https://web.archive.org/web/20260117124138/https://nicercode.github.io/guides/reports/) — Nice R Code guide from 2013 on assembling reproducible reports from these three tools (archived copy).
- [Compiling Reports from R Scripts](https://rmarkdown.rstudio.com/articles_report_from_r_script.html) — Posit article on turning a plain R script into a report.
- [Knitr's best hidden gem: spin](https://web.archive.org/web/20260125002922/https://deanattali.com/2015/03/24/knitrs-best-hidden-gem-spin/) — Dean Attali's post introducing knitr's spin function for writing reports from R scripts (archived copy).
- [Interchanging RMarkdown and "spinnable" R](https://www.r-bloggers.com/2018/11/interchanging-rmarkdown-and-spinnable-r/) — R-Bloggers post on moving between R Markdown documents and plain R scripts with spin.
- [rstudio/rmarkdown](https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown) — Source code and issue tracker for the rmarkdown package.

## Citations and bibliographies

- [Bibliographies and Citations](https://rmarkdown.rstudio.com/authoring_bibliographies_and_citations.html) — Posit guide to adding bibliographies and citations to R Markdown documents.
- [Citations in R Markdown](https://tutorials.inbo.be/tutorials/r_citations_markdown/) — Tutorial on citing publications and building bibliographies with RStudio's citation tools.
- [RStudio: Quick Guide to Citations](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zuuOYjE8m98) — Short YouTube guide to citations in RStudio.
- [citr](https://github.com/crsh/citr) — RStudio addin for inserting Markdown citations.
- [knitcitations](https://github.com/cboettig/knitcitations) — Package that generates citations for knitr Markdown and HTML documents.
- [RefManageR](https://github.com/ropensci/RefManageR) — Package for importing and managing bibliographic references from R.
- [grateful](https://github.com/Pakillo/grateful) — Package that helps you cite the R packages used in an analysis.

## Templates and output formats

- [rddj-template](https://github.com/grssnbchr/rddj-template) — Template for starting a reproducible R Markdown project in data journalism.
- [thesis_in_rmarkdown](https://github.com/rosannav/thesis_in_rmarkdown) — Example project for writing a thesis in R Markdown.
- [svm-r-markdown-templates](https://github.com/svmiller/svm-r-markdown-templates) — Collection of R Markdown templates for academic manuscripts, Beamer presentations, and syllabi.
- [pagedown](https://github.com/rstudio/pagedown) — Package for turning R Markdown HTML output into paged documents that print well.
- [officer](https://github.com/davidgohel/officer) — Package for creating Word and PowerPoint documents from R.
- [remedy](https://github.com/ThinkR-open/remedy) — RStudio addins that simplify writing Markdown.
- [tinytex](https://github.com/rstudio/tinytex) — Small LaTeX distribution for R Markdown PDF output; the [TinyTeX](../tinytex.html) page links to its website.
- [RPubs](https://rpubs.com/about/getting-started) — Getting-started page for publishing R Markdown documents online with RPubs.
